flagged.comment: Hard surface types are not shown in a comprehensive legend that distinguishes parking/circulation surfaces from buildings and vegetation areas. Hard surfaces are identified only through direct text callouts on the plan (e.g., 'Concrete Sidewalk', 'Decomposed Granite Walkway', 'Concrete Drive') without a coordinated legend using hatch patterns or distinct symbols.

Landscape plan shows proposed paving (H.1) and other landscape features (H.2-H.7) but does not clearly establish a legend that explicitly distinguishes parking/circulation surfaces from buildings and vegetation areas per FPCM requirements. While hatch patterns differentiate zones, the legend does not clearly isolate hard surface types for parking versus other hard surfaces.

Building overhangs and roof heights are not shown on the site plan or ESC plan to allow canopy conflict assessment. Detailed roof height and overhang information may be contained in architectural plans not provided in this site plan set. Site plan elevation notes list finished floor elevations but do not provide roof height or overhang projections.
areas: site plan (Sheet 9), ESC plan (Sheet 5), fire protection plan (Sheet 10)

flagged.comment: Building heights are documented in the Building Height Table (Sheet 9, ranging 33'-4.75" to 36'-1"), and fire apparatus clearance (14 feet) is noted as a general requirement on Sheet 3. However, specific building overhang dimensions are not explicitly shown on the site plan to allow canopy conflict assessment.

Existing structures are not dimensioned on the demolition plan. While property boundary lines include bearings and distances, the actual structural footprints slated for demolition (concrete slab, sidewalks, retaining walls) do not have length/width dimensions provided. Only property line bearings and specific linear measurements of demolition items (e.g., '79 LF Concrete Retaining Wall') are shown.

The existing demolished structure (slab FFE 686.8') is shown on the demolition plan but is not dimensioned with overall length and width measurements. Only the finished floor elevation is provided; structural footprint dimensions are absent.

No legend is provided on the demolition plan identifying all structures and improvements to be removed. While a 'Tree Legend' explains tree-related symbols (Trees to Remain, Heritage Trees, Protected Trees, etc.), there is no parallel demolition legend defining symbols or callout conventions for demolished structures and site improvements.

A Tree Legend is provided (Block 6, Sheet 8) distinguishing trees to remain, heritage trees, protected trees, and trees to be removed. However, no comprehensive legend is provided for structural demolition items (concrete, asphalt, utilities, etc.). Demolition items are identified by individual text callouts rather than a standardized symbol/legend system for structures and improvements to be removed.

Scope of demolition work is not clearly stated on the plan. Site Demolition Notes (items 1-10) outline procedural requirements but do not explicitly delineate what is included in this site demolition plan versus what may require separate demolition permits (e.g., structural building demolition vs. site utilities/hardscape demolition).

Sheet 8 contains Site Demolition Notes (Block 5) providing procedural instructions for tree protection, utility abandonment, and general demolition activities. However, no clear scope statement distinguishes what demolition work is included in this site plan versus work covered by separate demolition permits or other related projects.

Complex structures do not have detailed demolition callouts or notes specifying demolition methodology. While 'Demo Concrete Slab', 'Demo 79 LF Concrete Retaining Wall', and 'Abandon and Remove Grease Trap' are identified with callouts, there are no notes describing specific demolition methods, sequencing, or removal procedures for these complex items.

The existing structure (assisted living facility foundation slab) is shown for demolition but lacks detailed demolition callouts specifying demolition methodology. Site demolition notes reference hand-tool requirements for tree protection but do not address specific methodology for removal of the complex structure itself.

Plans do not clearly identify which improvements are proposed with this site plan versus improvements proposed under separate permits or related projects. While references exist to demolition permits, erosion control measures, and future certificate of occupancy requirements, there is no explicit statement clarifying the scope of work included in this specific site plan submission versus separate construction plans or phased work.
areas: site plan (Sheet 9), general notes (Sheet 3), cover sheet (Sheet 1)

flagged.comment: General release notes (Sheet 3, Block 12) state 'All improvements shall be made in accordance with the released site plan' and reference demolition permits separately. However, no comprehensive statement clearly identifies which specific improvements are included in this site plan versus improvements proposed under separate permits, construction plans, or related projects.
areas: Cover Sheet (Sheet 1), General Notes (Sheet 3), Site Plan (Sheet 9)

flagged.comment: Scope of work statement is not provided on the cover sheet or main site plan detailing proposed site work. While scattered references exist to site improvements (biofiltration pond, buildings, utilities), there is no consolidated narrative scope statement describing the overall proposed development, demolition, and infrastructure improvements.

Project scope (39 townhome units, 8 buildings) is embedded in the cover sheet data and site plan details but no dedicated 'Scope of Work' statement block clearly details the proposed site work, improvements, and construction activities in a comprehensive narrative format.

Construction Plan (C Plan) presence cannot be verified from the site plan set. Vertical construction is proposed (8 multi-family buildings), but no cross-reference or notation on the site plan indicates whether a separate C Plan has been submitted. This determination requires review of the complete permit application.

The project includes eight multi-family residential buildings (vertical construction) shown on the site plan. No dedicated Construction Plan (C Plan) sheet providing detailed vertical construction information appears in the 39-sheet site plan package. Sheets 22-28 are labeled 'Construction Details' but address utility infrastructure details, not vertical/building construction. It is unclear whether a C Plan must be part of the site plan submittal or is submitted separately with building permit applications.

All landscape elements are not labeled with required details on the main site plan. While trees are shown with symbols and reference numbers, specific landscape species and sizes are not labeled on Sheet 9. Trees are referenced to Sheet 32 for detailed list but not identified on the site plan itself.

No Building Information Table is included on the cover sheet. While a limited Austin Fire Department requirements table is shown, there is no comprehensive Building Information Table listing unit counts, gross floor area, parking requirements and provisions, and other project building data.

The relationship between existing site conditions (existing structures, stairs, egress from demolished building) and proposed paths cannot be verified on a single sheet. Existing conditions are shown on Sheet 4, proposed site plan on Sheet 9, and they are not cross-referenced. Field conditions relating existing site features to new pedestrian paths are not documented on the site plan.

All structures are not clearly labeled as either existing or proposed on the main site plan. Buildings are labeled as 'Bldg. 1' through 'Bldg. 8' with square footages but are not explicitly marked as 'proposed.' The word 'proposed' appears only in table descriptions (Site Data Table) but not on the building labels themselves.

Overall building dimensions (length × width) are not shown on the site plan. Instead of overall length and width dimensions, detailed perimeter wall segments are dimensioned (e.g., individual wall segments of 19.3', 10.2', 97.8', etc.). Simple overall length × width dimensions for each building are not provided.

Features are not comprehensively labeled with all relevant dimensions and labels on the site plan. While hard surfaces are labeled with text callouts and buildings show wall segment dimensions, landscape elements (species, sizes, planter dimensions) are not fully labeled with required details on the main site plan.

Landscape plan shows planting zones and identifies areas for parking lot landscaping (H.4) and street yard plantings (H.2, H.3) but does not provide specific dimensions (size and height) for individual proposed planters.

Required vertical clearance is not verified and documented on the site plan. No overhead obstructions (parking structures, canopies, overhead elements) are evident on this residential site requiring vertical clearance verification. Fire lanes are shown and dimensioned, but no overhead clearance requirements or dimensions are documented.

Structures proposed for demolition are not clearly indicated with consistent dashed lines or hatching. Demolition items are identified through direct text callouts in boxes (e.g., 'Demo Concrete Slab', 'Demo All Concrete Sidewalks') but the structural footprints themselves are not marked with distinct dashed outlines or hatching patterns to visually differentiate demolished areas from retained structures.

Topography is not shown at the required 2-foot contour intervals on-site. Instead, all sheets (existing conditions, grading plan, and ESC plan) show 1-foot contour intervals on-site and 1-foot intervals off-site. The required standard per Environmental Review Requirements Section 3 is 2-foot on-site and 50-foot off-site intervals. Off-site contours do not consistently extend a full 100 feet in all directions.
areas: existing conditions survey (Sheet 4), grading plan (Sheet 11), ESC plan (Sheet 5)
